title: ADMET Profiling of a Mitochondria-Focused Compound Library: Physicochemical Baselines, Membrane Permeability Classification, and Tier-Based Filtering for AI-Driven Drug Discovery
tldr:
### Problem
This research focuses on the ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) profiling of a mitochondria-focused compound library, aiming to establish physicochemical baselines, membrane permeability classification, and tier-based filtering for AI-driven drug discovery.

### Method
The study employs machine learning models to predict the ADMET properties of the compound library, classifying them based on their membrane permeability, and implementing a tier-based filtration system.

### Dataset / Benchmark
The research utilizes a mitochondria-focused compound library as its dataset for analysis.

### Key Findings
- The study presents physicochemical baselines for the mitochondria-focused compound library, providing valuable insights into their properties.
- Machine learning models successfully classified compounds based on membrane permeability, offering a potential tool for drug discovery.

title: STING, guided active learning for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials examined on Lithium Thiophosphate solid state electrolytes
tldr:
### Problem
The study investigates the application of Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) in predicting the structural properties of Lithium Thiophosphate (Li3PS5), a solid-state electrolyte material for lithium-ion batteries.

### Method
The authors propose STING, a guided active learning approach, to improve the accuracy and efficiency of MLIPs training by selectively focusing on informative data points.

### Dataset / Benchmark
The research utilizes experimental data from density functional theory calculations as the dataset for model training and validation.

### Key Findings
- STING significantly enhances the predictive performance of MLIPs, reducing mean absolute errors by 30% compared to traditional random sampling methods.
- The improved MLIPs accurately predict structural properties such as lattice parameters and vibrational frequencies of Li3PS5.
- The study demonstrates the potential of active learning strategies in optimizing MLIPs for drug discovery, computational chemistry, and molecular machine learning

title: Tokenizing loops of antibodies.
tldr:
### Problem
The problem addressed in this research revolves around predicting binding affinity of heavy chain variants and identifying similar H3 loops in antibodies, which are crucial for drug discovery, computational chemistry, and molecular machine learning.

### Method
The researchers have introduced ImmunoGlobulin LOOp Tokenizer (Igloo), a multimodal antibody loop tokenizer that encodes backbone dihedral angles and sequence. This method aims to improve protein foundation models and aid in antibody CDR design.

### Dataset / Benchmark
The performance of Igloo is evaluated against state-of-the-art protein encoding approaches, sequence-based and multimodal protein language models, and existing inverse folding models on 8 antibody-antigen targets and a structural antibody database.

### Key Findings
- Igloo outperforms the base protein language model on 8 out of 10 antibody-antigen targets in predicting binding affinity.

title: In Silico Pharmacological Profiling of MitoCorex Candidate Molecules: ADMET, Target Engagement, Selectivity, and Stability Analysis
tldr:
### Problem
This research focuses on the in silico pharmacological profiling of MitoCorex candidate molecules for drug discovery. The aim is to evaluate their Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity (ADMET), target engagement, selectivity, and stability.

### Method
The study employs molecular docking and machine learning techniques to predict the pharmacological properties of the MitoCorex candidate molecules.

### Dataset / Benchmark
The evaluation is based on a dataset of known drug compounds and their corresponding pharmacological properties.

### Key Findings
- The study successfully predicted the ADMET, target engagement, selectivity, and stability of the MitoCorex candidate molecules with high accuracy.
- The machine learning models developed showed promising performance in predicting the pharmacological properties of the candidate molecules.
- The results suggest that some of the MitoCorex candidate molecules have potential as drug leads.

title: Large Language Model-Guided Bayesian Optimization of Ag+ Doping in CdSe Nanoplatelets Enables Deterministic Optical Prediction across the Gamut
tldr:
### Problem
This research focuses on optimizing the properties of Cadmium Selenide (CdSe) nanoplatelets doped with Silver (Ag+), a crucial step in enhancing their optical properties for various applications. The challenge lies in achieving deterministic predictions and control over the optical properties across diverse conditions.

### Method
The study proposes a method combining Large Language Model (LLM)-guided Bayesian optimization to systematically explore the Ag+ doping levels in CdSe nanoplatelets, aiming to determine optimal conditions for predictable optical properties.

### Dataset / Benchmark
Experimental data from various Ag+-doped CdSe nanoplatelet samples serve as the dataset for evaluating the proposed method's performance.

### Key Findings
- The LLM-guided Bayesian optimization successfully identified optimal Ag+ doping levels, leading to improved optical properties in CdSe nanoplatelets.
- The method demonstrated robustness across a wide range of Ag+ doping concentrations

title: DSBD: Dual-Aligned Structural Basis Distillation for Graph Domain Adaptation
tldr:
### Problem
The research focuses on improving graph data distillation (GDA) for cross-domain generalization in drug discovery, computational chemistry, and molecular machine learning. Existing methods are primarily designed for in-domain settings and lack a differentiable structural adaptation substrate.

### Method
The proposed method, DSBD (Decoupled Structural Basis Distillation), adopts a bi-level optimization scheme to learn a continuous probabilistic structural basis. This approach decouples source-specific bias for cross-domain generalization through geometric and spectral alignment.

### Dataset / Benchmark
Experiments were conducted on both graph and image benchmarks.

### Key Findings
- DSBD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across diverse domain shifts.
- The decoupled inference paradigm mitigates source-specific structural bias by training a fresh model on the distilled basis, thereby improving generalization under topology shift.

title: Unleashing the power of DNA-encoded libraries for challenging targets in drug discovery.
tldr:
### Problem
The identification of ligands for challenging targets with featureless surfaces, high conformational plasticity, or shallow binding sites remains a significant hurdle in drug discovery.

### Method
This review discusses the strategic evolution of DNA-encoded library (DEL) technology over the past fifteen years as a transformative platform in early-stage drug discovery, focusing on its application against intractable targets such as GTPases, epigenetic regulators, phosphatases, protein-protein interaction (PPI), membrane proteins, and RNA.

### Dataset / Benchmark
The review provides pivotal case studies and methodological breakthroughs while critically examining aspects of DEL such as DNA-compatible chemistry, diversified library design, advanced selection strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI) integration.

title: Pan-Mitochondrial Privileged Scaffolds: Adenine, Pyridine, and a 7H-Purine Bioisostere as Multi-Target Fragments in the MitoCoreX Drug Discovery Campaign
tldr:
### Problem
The study aims to identify multi-target fragments for drug discovery campaigns focused on mitochondrial proteins, collectively referred to as MitoCoreX.

### Method
The researchers propose using a bioisostere of 7H-Purine, adenine, and pyridine as privileged scaffolds to discover pan-mitochondrial fragments.

### Dataset / Benchmark
The evaluation is based on the docking scores against a set of mitochondrial protein targets.

### Key Findings
- The study reveals that the proposed privileged scaffolds exhibit promising docking scores across various mitochondrial protein targets.
- Adenine and pyridine derivatives show significant potential as multi-target fragments for MitoCoreX drug discovery.
- The 7H-Purine bioisostere emerges as a valuable addition to the library of privileged scaffolds for mitochondrial drug discovery.

title: Next-generation Janus kinase inhibitors: Integrating synthetic innovation, structural biology, and computational design for precision drug discovery.
tldr:
### Problem
The problem lies in the limitations of current Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors, such as safety concerns, isoform selectivity issues, long-term tolerability problems, and off-target kinase interactions, which restrict their broader application.

### Method

The review outlines key opportunities and remaining challenges in developing next-generation JAK inhibitors for oncology, immunology, and chronic inflammatory diseases, focusing specifically on JAK2 and JAK3.

title: Drug-likeness prioritised selection identifies anti-Escherichia coli candidates confirmed by molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and antibacterial assays.
tldr:
### Problem
The research focuses on reducing late-stage attrition risk in rational antibacterial drug discovery by addressing the imbalance between antibacterial potency and developability in cephalosporin discovery against Escherichia coli.

### Method
A comprehensive screening strategy guided by the principle of maximum drug-likeness was developed, combined with a five-fold property-spectrum scoring mechanism (S5F) for multidimensional and quantitative prioritization of candidates based on overall developability.

### Dataset / Benchmark
An integrated evaluation framework was established consisting of 33 independent predictive submodels across five dimensions: physicochemical properties, pharmacokinetics, safety, efficacy, and stability.

title: Transfer Learning for Loan Recovery Prediction under Distribution Shifts with Heterogeneous Feature Spaces
tldr:
### Problem
Transfer learning (TL) for risk rating (RR) forecasting in small data regimes can be challenging due to potential distributional shifts and heterogeneity between source and target feature spaces.

### Method
The study proposes using a Fine-tuned Multimodal Distribution-aware Transformer (FT–MDN–Transformer) model for RR prediction, which accommodates schema heterogeneity and models full conditional distributions.

### Dataset / Benchmark
The research is based on both real-data and simulation settings.
